summary: The code parses URL parameters to display a personalized greeting via innerHTML and evaluates a mathematical formula using the dangerous eval function. Overall, it has severe security vulnerabilities due to untrusted input handling.

issues.description: The function calculate passes the user-supplied formula parameter directly to eval(), allowing arbitrary code execution.
issues.suggestion: Remove eval() and use a safe math parsing library to evaluate expressions.

issues.description: User-supplied input from window.location.search is concatenated directly into box.innerHTML via showGreeting, allowing DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).
issues.suggestion: Use box.textContent = 'Welcome, ' + name + '!'; instead of innerHTML.

suggestions: Validate and sanitize all inputs originating from URL parameters before processing them.
Avoid using innerHTML when assigning plain text values to DOM elements.
Never use eval() for processing user input or evaluating mathematical formulas.
